signals.title: A Study on the Mechanism and Ways to Improve New-Quality Productivity of Enterprises Driven by AI and the Digital Economy
signals.abstract: With the deep development of the digital economy and the accelerated iteration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, the formation and development of enterprise new quality productive forces have attracted increasing attention from academia and practice. Based on enterprises as the micro-subject, this paper constructs a theoretical analysis framework for the "dual-wheel drive of AI and the digital economy" and explores the formation mechanism and the path to enhancing the synergistic empowerment of enterprise these forces. The research finds that AI and the digital economy are not simply parallel drivers, but form a synergistic empowerment effect through a triple interactive mechanism of "technology-factor-organization." AI technology reshapes the technological boundary of the production function, while the digital economy reconstructs the allocation logic of production factors.

signals.abstract: Abstract This study examines the role of multinational enterprise (MNE) subsidiaries in facilitating environmental upgrading in value chains, with a specific focus on the salmon aquaculture sector. Addressing the critical challenge of Scope 3 emissions, this research investigates the dynamics between a French food MNE’s UK subsidiary (Company X) in UK, acting as a Tier 1 supplier, and its lower-tier suppliers in Scotland and Norway. We explore how do multinational enterprise subsidiaries act as bridging mechanisms to mediate sustainability mandates and local institutional contexts, driving environmental upgrading and addressing Scope 3 emissions in the context of salmon value chains. signals.title: Digital transformation and artificial intelligence in organic supply chains: A systematic review with insights from South Tamil Nadu
signals.venue: Journal of Management Research and Analysis
signals.abstract: Organic agriculture is growing rapidly in India, yet organic supply chains remain structurally fragmented, particularly in smallholder-dominated regions such as South Tamil Nadu. signals.title: From Indenture to Electronics: Brokered Labor Regimes in Johor, Malaysia
signals.abstract: Abstract This article develops the concept of a brokered dormitory labor regime (BDLR) to analyze Johor, Malaysia’s electrical and electronics export-processing zones, where debt-financed recruitment, deceptive contracting, and restricted mobility synchronize labor turnover with the accelerating demand for semiconductor manufacturing driven by artificial intelligence. Two intermediaries, the labor agent and the kadar, secure this synchronization by controlling workers’ social reproduction. Tracing this regime’s genealogy to the nineteenth-century kangani and kangchu systems in the Straits Settlements, the article argues that the BDLR reactivates a colonial infrastructure of coerced migrant labor, revealing a recurring pattern of asynchronous synchronization between capital and labor across successive industrial revolutions.

signals.title: Public technical disclosure of AI implementation in finance: Python-framed evidence from 253 NYSE-listed financial companies
signals.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) claims in public markets increasingly raise disclosure, comparability, and investor-protection questions, yet evidence on how listed financial firms publicly describe implementation remains fragmented and difficult to compare. This study examines public technical disclosure rather than internal adoption by constructing a screened, exchange-bounded corpus for 253 NYSE-listed financial companies. signals.title: Healthcare That Learns
signals.abstract: Healthcare has more evidence, data, and artificial intelligence (AI) than ever. A risk model can flag a patient, a dashboard can reveal a gap, and a guideline can recommend the next step. Los cambios estructurales son específicos de cada secto

signals.title: Integrated territorial investments and the ‘Europeanization' of spatial planning and territorial development in Greece: weakening institutional dualism?
signals.abstract: The paper explores the dynamics of the Europeanization of spatial planning and territorial development in Greece following the introduction of the integrated territorial investment (ITI) mechanism. These dynamics evolve in the context of so-called ‘development programming’ and ‘regulatory planning’ systems which mostly operate in parallel to each other – a case of institutional dualism. Based on the analysis of interviews with experts and institutional actors, and of relevant documentation (policies, strategies, laws, etc.), the paper argues that the introduction of the EU’s new territorial delivery mechanisms strengthen local capacity to implement territorial development plans and may potentially weaken institutional dualism.

signals.title: R&D Efficiency and Business Sector Spending in European Regions: Lessons From the Conditional Efficiency Approach
signals.abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigates the relationship between business R&D spending and R&D efficiency across 256 European regions. Using patent applications and publications as outputs and overall R&D expenditure as input, the analysis reveals significant efficiency disparities between and within countries. The Netherlands boasts top performers, while Greece and Eastern Europe lag. To shed light on these differences, a fully nonparametric conditional efficiency approach is applied to study the relationship between R&D efficiency and the share of the business sector in total R&D spending. Results indicate an optimal business R&D share of around 61%, beyond which efficiency declines.

signals.title: Institutional quality, structural change and regional development in the EU
signals.abstract: This study examines the drivers of regional economic development in the European Union over the period 2000–2021. We focus on conventional determinants, various sectoral covariates and the role of local institutions. Controlling for spatial spillover effects and potential endogeneity, we confirm that investment, human capital and specialisation in service activities are key drivers of regional development. In addition, the quality of government (QoG) is a significant predictor of regional development. In line with theoretical arguments, impartiality has a higher impact on economic growth than the quality of public services and control of corruption.
